title: Entropy growth rate of the objective
statement:
Fix $0 < \tau < 1/2$, and let $(t_n)$ be a sequence of natural numbers and $(a_n)$ a sequence of reals such that $t_n/n \to \tau$ and, for all sufficiently large $n$, the point $a_n$ lies strictly below every real zero of the Krawtchouk polynomial $K_{t_n}^{(n)}$. Then the truncated Christoffel--Darboux kernel evaluated at $(a_n, 0)$ grows at rate at most $H(\tau)$, in the sense that
\[
  \limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n}\log_2 \Phi_{n,t_n}(a_n, 0) \;\le\; H(\tau),
\]
where $H$ is the binary entropy function in base $2$.
hypotheses_covered: eventually a_n lies strictly below every real zero of K_{t_n}^{(n)}
